niche: online spiritual and shadow work courses
prompt_text: What are the best online courses for learning shadow work and spiritual practice?
answer_verbatim:
“Best” depends on whether you want a psychology-based approach, a daily contemplative practice, or a particular religious tradition. For a grounded starting point, I’d shortlist these:

### Shadow work
- **[Encounters with the Shadow: Introduction to Jungian Shadow Work](https://jungplatform.com/courses)** — James Hollis introduces Jung’s idea of the shadow and how it can show up in everyday life. A good first course if you want a clear, depth-psychology framework.
- **[Engage the Shadow](https://jungplatform.com/course/engage-the-shadow)** — A broader course with ten depth-psychology teachers. It covers personal and collective shadow, relationships, dreams, and practical reflection tools. Better if you want several perspectives rather than one instructor.
- **[Shadow Work](https://jungian.directory/courses/shadow-work/)** — A self-paced option with audio lectures, readings, and exercises from the Jungian Center for the Spiritual Sciences.
- **[Meeting and Romancing Your Shadow](https://www.spiritualityandpractice.com/ecourses/course/filter/on-demand/retreats-on-classic-practices)** — A more explicitly spiritual, reflective option listed by Spirituality & Practice.

### Spiritual practice
- **[InterSpiritual Meditation](https://www.spiritualityandpractice.com/ecourses/course/view/103/interspiritual-meditation)** — A short, daily-email course drawing on practices from multiple traditions, including gratitude, compassion, mindfulness, and meditation. A reasonable choice if you want a flexible, nonsectarian routine.
- **[The Power of Awareness](https://www.soundstrue.com/collections/spirituality)** — A mindfulness-oriented program from Jack Kornfield and Tara Brach, highlighted by Sounds True as an accessible introduction.
- **Stanford Continuing Studies: Cultivating Calm: Exploring Spiritual Wellness** — A five-week online course combining contemplative practices such as mindfulness meditation and poetic reflection. Check the current term and enrollment dates.

**My simplest recommendation:** start with *Encounters with the Shadow* for shadow work and *InterSpiritual Meditation* for a regular practice. If you prefer a more structured, multi-teacher exploration, choose *Engage the Shadow*.

A note of care: shadow work can bring up painful memories or intense emotions. Treat courses as educational, not therapy; go slowly, skip exercises that feel destabilizing, and consider working with a licensed mental-health professional if trauma or significant distress comes up. Check each provider’s current price, access period, and course dates before enrolling.
